body: EMS companies assemble electronics for brand owners: mobiles, TVs, IT hardware and wearables, plus industrial, auto and defence boards. Profit is a thin conversion margin (2–4% EBITDA for mobile assembly, 8–15% for industrial/auto boards) on huge pass-through revenue, so RoCE comes from asset turns and working-capital speed. PLI incentives have been a material share of profit. Backward integration (displays, camera modules, PCBs under ECMS) offers higher margins. Key metrics: revenue growth by segment, EBITDA margin and absolute EBITDA, RoCE, net working capital days, customer concentration, PLI income as a share of EBITDA, export share, value addition %, and capex for component plants. Cycle drivers: smartphone demand and brand outsourcing decisions (Apple, Samsung, Chinese brands seeking JV partners), PLI scheme tenure (mobile PLI ended FY26), ECMS component incentives, US tariffs and China+1, and GST and tariff duty structure. Lead indicators: MeitY production and export data, ICEA mobile export data, Commerce Ministry HS 8517 exports, ECMS approval notifications, client announcements. Winners (Dixon over 2018–25) made early bets on mobile PLI, ran a capital-light, high asset-turn model and moved up into components. Losers suffered customer loss (single-client concentration) or working-capital blow-outs. Kaynes in 2025 showed how accounting-disclosure concerns can hit a high-multiple stock. Valuation: P/E 60–120x at the 2024–25 peak. Nov 2026: Dixon's Q2 FY27 revenue rose sharply (+35% to +47%; sources differ), but operating margin fell to 2.7% from 3.8% as mobile PLI ended, PAT fell 45% on lower other income, and ₹1,110 cr of PLI receivables are outstanding. Traps: PLI-inflated margins, and revenue growth with falling RoCE.

data.business_model: Contract manufacturing; thin conversion margin on pass-through revenue; PLI/ECMS subsidies; component backward integration.
data.current_state_nov_2026: Dixon Q2 FY27: revenue up strongly (sources give +35% to ₹37,341 cr or +47% to ₹21,794 cr; unreconciled), PBT +9%, PAT ₹411 cr (−45% on lower other income), op margin 2.7% vs 3.8% after mobile PLI ended; ₹1,110 cr PLI receivables outstanding; FY27 ex-Vivo guidance ~₹56,000 cr; display JV commercial production targeted Q4 FY27.
data.cycle_drivers: Smartphone/consumer electronics demand, brand sourcing shifts, PLI/ECMS policy, tariffs/China+1, component import duties.
key_metrics: Revenue growth by segment (mobile, consumer, IT hardware, industrial)
traps: Capitalising PLI subsidies as permanent margin
Disclosure/RPT red flags at high multiples
data.valuation: P/E 60–120x at 2024–25 peaks for Dixon/Kaynes; EV/EBITDA 40–70x. Pre-PLI (2017–19) Dixon ~30–40x. Value usually sits in EBITDA growth and RoCE, not revenue.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Global brand (design, IP, demand) -> EMS assembler -> component suppliers (chips, displays, camera modules; mostly imported, highest margins) -> distribution. Brand owners and component makers take most of the profit; assembly is low-margin but scalable.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: early policy positioning, capital-light, multi-client, credible component integration, conservative accounting. Losers: one-client dependence, receivables (incl. PLI dues) build-up, RPT/disclosure issues, margin collapse after subsidy roll-off.

title: Sector playbook: EMS and electronics manufacturing
